title: Interteam Dependency Lifecycle Playbook and Quarterly Commit Protocol
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Cross-team dependencies during roadmap planning cause missed ship dates, uncoordinated rollouts, and last-minute scope cuts. Existing dependency signals are fragmented (sheets, Slack, ad-hoc PR comments) and lack a standard lifecycle, ownership rules, and measurable SLAs.

Goal: Define an operational playbook and lightweight data model to track dependencies across Product, Eng, Design, Security, and Infra so that every dependency moves through a predictable lifecycle with clear owners, mitigations, and quarterly commitment windows. The outcome should reduce unplanned scope drop >25% for priority OKR initiatives and shorten resolution time for blocking dependencies by 40% within two quarters.
success_metrics: % of priority OKR dependencies that reach Committed state before cycle start >= 85%
Median time from dependency open to mitigation plan <= 10 business days
Reduction in last-minute scope removals for committed initiatives >= 25% quarter-over-quarter
% of dependencies with explicit owner and fallback >= 95%
proposed_solution: Introduce a 6-state dependency lifecycle: Identified -> Triage -> Committed -> Blocked -> In-flight -> Resolved

Quarterly Commit Protocol: during roadmap freeze, stakeholders must accept or decline dependency commitments; acceptance creates an immutable commitment window for engineering planning and capacity allocation

Enforce explicit fields on every dependency: owner (team/person), impact (low/med/high), SLA for acknowledgement (48 hours), SLA for mitigation plan (10 business days), fallback plan, verification criteria
Lightweight dependency score (0-10) combining customer impact, blocker status, and implementation effort to prioritize escalations
Automate signals: sync Linear dependencies with a shared dependency dashboard in Console and a Confluence commitment register; generate weekly digest to PM/EM/Design leads
Escalation ladder: owner -> PM -> Head of Eng/Design/Security -> CTO for high-impact unresolved items after escalation SLA
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Run a pilot with 3 cross-functional initiatives in Cycle 2026-Q1; collect feedback and adjust lifecycle states and SLAs
Phase 2 (4 weeks): Implement Linear templates and webhook to populate Console dependency dashboard; add validation for required fields when marking Committed
Phase 3 (ongoing): Enforce Quarterly Commit Protocol at roadmap freeze for all priority OKRs; build automation for reminders and escalations
Phase 4 (Q2): Measure success metrics and iterate on scoring weights and SLA thresholds
acceptance_criteria: Linear dependency template requiring owner, impact, SLA fields, and fallback exists and is used by pilot initiatives
Console dashboard shows live dependency state and SLA timers for pilot initiatives
Three pilot initiatives complete a full lifecycle (Identified->Resolved) using the playbook and provide structured feedback
Quarterly Commit Protocol documented in Confluence and adopted by PM/EM leads for roadmap freeze

2026-03-07: Draft data model posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RRI/Dependency+Lifecycle+Model. Feedback from Security: add explicit data retention note for KMS-related deps. Action: update model by 2026-03-09.

2026-03-10: Prototype Console dependency dashboard wireframes shared in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbC-deps-dashboard. Design feedback: add SLA countdown and color-coded risk column. Estimate 4 points for frontend effort.

2026-03-12: Created GitHub stub repo for dependency scoring service and webhook integration: https://github.com/redwoodinc/dependency-tracker/pull/3. PR includes schema and sample webhook payloads. TODO: ENG to implement ack SLA timer (48h).

2026-03-14: Update: pilot kickoff retro scheduled 2026-03-28 to collect metrics from first two weeks. Added follow-up tasks to define escalation emails and PagerDuty policy for high-impact Blocked state.
notes: Trade-offs considered: strict enforcement of Committed state vs. forcing teams into false commitments. Decision: keep human sign-off but required fields and automation to increase visibility.
Potential blockers: infra telemetry to surface capacity constraints; plan to surface estimated GPU availability per quarter as a signal to influence Commit decisions.
Follow-ups: add dependency maturity badge in roadmap UI, and link dependency resolution to release notes automation in Console
